title: Terraform Cloud, Enterprise & Team Workflows
description: Mastery of Terraform Cloud/Enterprise: workspaces, VCS triggers, speculative plans, agents, run triggers, and private registries.

questions.question: What is the difference between a workspace in the Terraform CLI and a workspace in Terraform Cloud?
options: A. There is no difference; they are identical.

B. In the CLI, workspaces are simply alternate named state files in the same directory. In Terraform Cloud, workspaces contain state, environment variables, HCL variables, run histories, VCS connections, and access controls.
C. CLI workspaces are only for AWS; Cloud workspaces are for Azure.
D. Cloud workspaces do not store state.
questions.explanation: In CLI, a workspace is just a separate state file. In Terraform Cloud, a workspace is an entire execution environment with its own variables, state history, VCS triggers, team permissions, and run queues.

questions.question: What are the three execution modes supported by Terraform Cloud workspaces?
options: A. Fast, Normal, Slow
B. Remote, Local, Agent
C. Direct, Indirect, Proxy
D. Cloud, On-Premise, Hybrid
questions.explanation: Terraform Cloud workspaces support three execution modes: Remote (runs on HashiCorp hosted runners), Local (runs on the user's CLI and syncs state to Cloud), and Agent (runs on self-hosted agents within private networks).

questions.question: What is a 'VCS-driven workflow' in Terraform Cloud?
options: A. Terraform runs exclusively inside Git submodules.
B. A workflow where Terraform Cloud is connected to a version control repository (GitHub, GitLab), automatically triggering plans on Pull Requests and applies on merges to main.
C. A workflow where developers run plans via email.
D. Manually running terraform apply on a laptop.
questions.explanation: In VCS-driven workflows, Terraform Cloud monitors repository webhooks. Committing to branches triggers speculative plans, and merging to the default branch triggers an apply queue.

questions.question: What feature allows you to share reusable sets of variables across multiple workspaces in Terraform Cloud?
options: A. Global tfvars files
B. Variable Sets
C. Shared Workspaces
D. Organization Secrets
questions.explanation: 'Variable Sets' in Terraform Cloud allow defining groups of environment or Terraform variables once and applying them automatically to all or selected workspaces across an organization.

questions.question: What are 'Run Triggers' in Terraform Cloud?
options: A. Cron jobs that run every hour.
B. A mechanism that automatically triggers a run in a downstream workspace whenever an upstream workspace successfully finishes applying changes.
C. Webhooks that alert Slack.
D. Shell scripts that execute during init.
questions.explanation: Run Triggers establish workspace dependencies. For example, applying changes to a 'networking' workspace can automatically trigger a plan in an 'applications' workspace.

questions.question: When does Cost Estimation occur during a Terraform Cloud run?
options: A. After the apply has finished and billing is calculated.
B. Between the plan phase and the apply phase, allowing teams to review monthly cost impacts before committing changes.
C. Only once a month.
D. During terraform init.
questions.explanation: Cost Estimation runs immediately after the plan is generated. It calculates delta monthly costs for supported cloud resources (AWS, Azure, GCP) so operators can review cost impacts before approving the apply.

questions.question: What is the purpose of 'Cloud Agents' in Terraform Cloud?
options: A. Chatbots that answer Terraform questions.
B. Lightweight binaries deployed inside private, isolated data centers or VPCs that execute Terraform plans and applies without exposing private networks to the public internet.
C. Background cron jobs.
D. Customer support agents.
questions.explanation: Terraform Cloud Agents enable managing infrastructure in isolated private networks (e.g. on-prem or private VPCs) without opening inbound firewall ports to the public internet.

questions.question: What is the difference between Terraform Cloud and Terraform Enterprise?
options: A. Terraform Cloud is a SaaS hosted by HashiCorp; Terraform Enterprise is a self-hosted, customer-managed private installation for enterprises with strict data residency requirements.
B. Terraform Enterprise is open-source; Terraform Cloud is closed-source.
C. Terraform Cloud does not support Sentinel.
D. There is no difference.
questions.explanation: Terraform Cloud is HashiCorp's fully managed multi-tenant SaaS offering. Terraform Enterprise is the self-hosted distribution that customers install in their own private data centers or clouds.

questions.question: Which workflow allows developers to run 'terraform plan' and 'terraform apply' locally on their laptops while execution runs remotely on Terraform Cloud?
options: A. CLI-driven workflow
B. API-driven workflow
C. VCS-driven workflow
D. Docker workflow
questions.explanation: In a CLI-driven workflow, developers use familiar terminal commands ('terraform plan', 'terraform apply'), but execution streams live output from remote Terraform Cloud runners.

questions.question: How do you configure the Terraform CLI to log in to Terraform Cloud / HCP Terraform?
options: A. terraform auth
B. terraform login
C. terraform connect
D. terraform signup
questions.explanation: 'terraform login' opens a browser window to generate an API user token and saves it locally in '~/.terraform.d/credentials.tfrc.json'.

questions.question: In Terraform Cloud, who can override a 'Soft Mandatory' Sentinel policy violation?
options: A. Any team member with read access.
B. Only users belonging to an authorized team with policy override permissions.
C. No one; soft mandatory policies can never be overridden.
D. The cloud provider.
questions.explanation: Soft Mandatory policies halt execution, but permit authorized administrators or designated compliance team members to override the block and proceed with apply.

questions.question: What is the Private Module Registry in Terraform Cloud?
options: A. A registry visible to all HashiCorp customers.
B. A secure, internal registry allowing organizations to curate, version, and share approved internal modules across teams while keeping source code private.
C. An npm mirror.
D. A Docker hub clone.
questions.explanation: The Private Module Registry enables enterprise teams to publish internal modules with semantic versioning and auto-generated documentation, accessible only to organization members.

questions.question: What is an 'API-driven workflow' in Terraform Cloud?
options: A. Using Terraform to build REST APIs.
B. Orchestrating workspace runs, variable updates, and applies via external automation tools (like Jenkins, GitHub Actions, or custom scripts) using Terraform Cloud's REST API.
C. An obsolete feature.
D. Sourcing providers via API.
questions.explanation: An API-driven workflow allows third-party orchestrators (like Jenkins, CircleCI, or custom scripts) to programmatically create workspaces, upload configuration archives, and monitor runs via API.

questions.question: What block in HCL connects a local root module directly to Terraform Cloud?
options: A. cloud block: terraform { cloud { organization = "org" workspaces { name = "ws" } } }
B. connect block
C. remote_exec block
D. registry block
questions.explanation: Terraform 1.1+ introduced the dedicated 'cloud' block inside the 'terraform' block: 'terraform { cloud { organization = "my-org" workspaces { name = "my-app-prod" } } }'.

questions.question: Can the 'cloud' block and a 'backend' block be declared simultaneously in the same configuration?
options: A. Yes, cloud mirrors to backend.
B. No, 'cloud' and 'backend' are mutually exclusive; declaring both produces an error.
C. Only if using local backend.
D. Yes, in Terraform Enterprise.
questions.explanation: The 'cloud' block is a specialized cloud backend integration. Defining both 'cloud' and 'backend' blocks simultaneously is forbidden.

questions.question: What is 'Drift Detection' in Terraform Cloud?
options: A. Alerts when code formatting is inconsistent.
B. Scheduled background assessments that regularly refresh state against real-world infrastructure and notify teams if out-of-band changes occur.
C. Automatic deletion of modified resources.
D. Upgrading provider versions overnight.
questions.explanation: Health / Drift Assessment runs periodic scheduled refreshes without user intervention, alerting teams via Slack, email, or webhooks if infrastructure drifts from code.

questions.question: How does Terraform Cloud prevent conflicting concurrent runs in the same workspace?
options: A. It merges concurrent runs together automatically.
B. It queues subsequent runs sequentially; only one active run can execute at a time per workspace.
C. It cancels the earlier run.
D. It generates duplicate cloud resources.
questions.explanation: Terraform Cloud workspaces serialize execution: if a run is currently applying, subsequent runs are placed into a queue until the active run finishes and the state lock is released.

questions.question: What is an 'Organization' in Terraform Cloud?
options: A. A Git branch.
B. The top-level shared workspace container representing a company or business unit, containing workspaces, teams, policies, and registries.
C. A provider plugin.
D. An AWS account.
questions.explanation: An Organization is the top-level tenancy boundary in Terraform Cloud. Workspaces, team memberships, billing, variable sets, and policies all belong to an Organization.

questions.question: Can you use Terraform Cloud for free?
options: A. No, it requires an enterprise subscription.
B. Yes, HashiCorp provides a Free Tier that includes state management, VCS integration, and up to 500 managed resources.
C. Only for a 14-day trial.
D. Only for academic use.
questions.explanation: Terraform Cloud offers a generous Free tier suitable for individuals and small teams, including remote state storage, VCS triggers, and up to 500 managed resources.

questions.question: How do you lock a Terraform Cloud workspace to prevent any applies during maintenance?
options: A. Click 'Lock Workspace' in the workspace settings, which stops all future runs from executing until unlocked.
B. Delete the workspace.
C. Disconnect Git.
D. Set plan = false in HCL.
questions.explanation: Administrators can manually lock a workspace in the UI/API, preventing any queued or newly triggered runs from applying until manually unlocked.

questions.question: What is the function of the 'Team & Governance' tier in Terraform Cloud?
options: A. Adds Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), team-based workspace permissions, and Sentinel/OPA policy management.
B. Writes code for developers.
C. Decreases cloud hosting costs.
D. Uninstalls unused modules.
questions.explanation: Governance capabilities allow enterprises to enforce granular RBAC (assigning teams to workspaces with read, plan, or admin rights) and Policy as Code compliance gates.

questions.question: Where does Terraform Cloud store previous versions of your state files?
options: A. Only the latest state is kept; prior versions are discarded.
B. It automatically maintains an immutable historical ledger of every state version produced by every run, viewable in the 'States' tab.
C. In a local .bak file.
D. On floppy disk.
questions.explanation: Terraform Cloud stores every state version generated over the life of a workspace, allowing teams to audit changes, view historical diffs, or roll back if necessary.

questions.question: What is a 'Workspace Tag' in Terraform Cloud?
options: A. An AWS tag applied to EC2.
B. Metadata labels applied to workspaces for filtering, searching, and scoping variable sets.
C. Git commit tag.
D. A compiler flag.
questions.explanation: Workspace tags are organizational labels in Terraform Cloud (e.g. 'env:prod', 'team:payments') used to filter workspaces and assign targeted Variable Sets.

questions.question: What is 'No-Code Provisioning' in HCP Terraform?
options: A. Writing bash scripts instead of Terraform.
B. A feature enabling non-technical users to deploy standardized, pre-approved modules from the Private Registry via a web form without writing HCL.
C. Using ChatGPT to write plans.
D. An obsolete plugin.
questions.explanation: No-Code Provisioning allows platform teams to publish curated modules so developers or operations staff can provision standard environments through a self-service UI.

questions.question: In a VCS-driven workspace, what happens when you create a branch and open a Pull Request?
options: A. Terraform applies the changes immediately to production.
B. A speculative plan runs and the results are posted directly to the PR comments without modifying state.
C. Nothing happens until the branch is merged.
D. State file is destroyed.
questions.explanation: Speculative plans run automatically on PRs, giving reviewers immediate insight into whether code passes plan, what resources will be created/modified, and whether policies pass.
